new_structural_lemma.name: GLOBAL_MINCUT_SINGLETON_COMPONENT_FULL_CUT_VISIBILITY
new_structural_lemma.statement: Let B be the globally minimum variable-only cut selected over all constraint-node pairs in a connected incidence graph. If removing B leaves every constraint-bearing component with exactly one relation, then every relation contains every variable of B that is shared with the rest of the instance; under the frozen full-cut carrier scope this implies each component relation exposes the full B.
new_structural_lemma.proof_sketch: Assume relation R omits b in B. Because R is a singleton component after deleting B, every variable incident to R but not in B is private to R; otherwise a surviving shared variable would connect R to another constraint after deleting B. Hence all shared-variable paths from R to any other constraint enter through variables in scope(R) intersect B, whose cardinality is < |B|. Deleting those variables separates R from the rest, producing a variable cut smaller than B for a constraint pair, contradicting global minimality of B.
new_structural_lemma.effect: The v1 PARTIAL_CUT_VISIBILITY negative control was logically incompatible with the other scope obligations and is removed rather than repaired. Full-cut visibility becomes a derived obligation checked from graph structure.
